texts: good. both sides are bare kinds, so it lands as a single kind-level requirement between distillation and sea-water at generic strength.

bad: the mass subject "Salt" is dropped straight into the doer slot of one denied replacing event, so the parse denies a single occasion rather than stating the general rule that salt never substitutes — the generic claim the sentence actually makes. Recast it as a copular denial, the shape a bare kind subject is licensed to take: "In distillation, salt is not a substitute for sea-water." The domain phrase then attaches as the condition on a kind-level claim instead of hanging off an invented event.
good. the "Cauldron Hall" premodifier links to the store by a loose association rather than an invented containment, the store is the doer of the drawing, and the tide-pools are its source.

bad: "harbor mouth" is fused into a single kind, so the harbour itself never gets a symbol and the mouth's belonging to it is lost; a stray extra atom also types "sea-water" as a kind of water on a symbol nothing else in the parse uses. Write the part-whole out with "of", which forces the two entities apart and gives the harbour its own record: "The sea-water store draws from the deep ebb at the mouth of the harbor." The rest — the ebb as the source, "deep" split off as its own property, and the "at" containment — is right as it stands.

mixed: the group of cisterns, the count of three, the position at the back of Cauldron Hall and the holding all come out right, but the parse also derives that EACH of the three cisterns holds the sea-water, where the sentence means the three hold it between them. Add the collective marker, which the translator reads directly and which switches off the per-member reading: "Three stone cisterns at the back of Cauldron Hall hold the sea-water between them."
